title: The fuel-line equation
caption: Aggregate storage bandwidth must deliver every global batch inside the step window: accelerator count times batch bytes divided by step time. For the tokenized-text job it comes out to ~2.7 MB/s fleet-wide, while the same inequality on an image corpus demands hundreds of GB/s. Compute upgrades shrink the denominator and raise the requirement.

symbols.meaning: input bytes one worker consumes per step
step time, the delivery window (~4.64 s modeled)

title: The stall frontier
caption: In a fully overlapped pipeline the fraction of time compute is active equals the ratio of delivered to demanded bandwidth, capped at one. Below the knee the fleet starves linearly; above it the fleet is fed. Prefetch depth hides latency variance but cannot move a sustained rate deficit — only bandwidth or a more compact representation moves the knee.

symbols.meaning: fraction of wall-clock time accelerators are computing
bandwidth the storage path actually delivers

title: Two-phase checkpoint cost
caption: The synchronous pause is only the local-stripe write: the node's ~9.6 GB shard at four-drive RAID-0 bandwidth. The durable copy to the parallel file system (~2.45 s) runs asynchronously against later steps. A one-second pause would still cost ~22% of a 4.64 s step, but only ~0.17% of the ten-minute interval.

symbols.meaning: per-node checkpoint shard (~9.6 GB of the 2,450 GB save)
synchronous pause vs asynchronous durable copy time

title: Lifetime checkpoint volume
caption: The 14 byte-per-parameter resumable contract makes one save 2,450 GB; at ten-minute intervals over the 30-day window that is 4,320 saves and ~10.6 PB of writes, over a thousand times the epoch's 6 TB read volume. The write path, not the corpus, sizes the storage system.

symbols.meaning: bytes per checkpoint (params x 14 B for resumable Adam)

title: Delivered rate under caching
caption: With ~88% of the corpus held in the local RAID-0 cache, mean delivered rate lands ~16 GB/s: hits stream at local-stripe speed while misses pay the node's parallel-filesystem share, ~7x slower per byte. Locality-aware staging converts shared-service bandwidth into per-node bandwidth for the working set.

symbols.meaning: cache hit rate (~0.88 for the multimodal corpus)
local stripe vs the node's share of the PFS (~7x spread)

title: Movement is the meter
caption: Object storage prices residence and movement separately: 1 PB at \$0.02/GB-month is \$240k/year of rent, but ten full reads at \$0.09/GB is \$900k of egress. The cost question is how often the bytes move, not how many exist — the same asymmetry that makes checkpoints the dominant traffic makes egress the dominant bill.

symbols.meaning: bytes transferred out of the store per year
